b) If Θ is a variety of groups, then let Θ0 denote the category of all free groups
of finite rank in Θ. It is proved (G. Mashevitzky, B. Plotkin, E. Plotkin J. Algebra,
282 (2004), 490–512) that if Θ is the variety of all groups, then every automorphism
of the category Θ0 is an inner one. The same is true if Θ is the variety of all nilpotent
groups of class ⩽ d, for d ⩾ 2 (A. Tsurkov, Int. J. Algebra Comput., 17 (2007),
1273–1281). Is this true for the varieties of solvable groups? of metabelian groups?
    An automorphism φ of a category is called inner if it is isomorphic to the identity
automorphism. Let s : 1 → φ be a function defining this isomorphism. Then for
every object A we have an isomorphism sA : A → φ(A) and for any morphism of
objects µ : A → B we have φ(µ) = sB µs−1   A .                              B. I. Plotkin
